purpose: Sections 3/6/13/14/33: the production-domain concept design, and why it generalizes existing models rather than duplicating them.
chosenName: ClaimReviewItem (+ ClaimReviewObservation append-only detection log + ClaimReviewDecision append-only resolution-lifecycle log)
whyThisNameNotClaimReviewEvent: The spec's own suggested names (ClaimReviewEvent / SemanticReviewItem) describe a single occurrence; this architecture's core dedup requirement (Section 11: 'discovery -> compiler failure -> verification failure may remain ONE open claim-level review item with multiple observations') means the PRIMARY persisted row is an ITEM (one per claim, long-lived, mutable status), not an EVENT (one per detection, immutable). Calling the primary row ClaimReviewItem and its append-only children ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision keeps this distinction explicit in the schema itself, mirroring the existing, proven ExtractionCandidate (item) + CandidateReviewEvent (append-only log) split already shipped in this codebase.

existingModelsAudited.scope: An attorney's review of a golden-test/permission/legal conclusion - human-authored legal analysis, not a pipeline-detected claim-level safety gap.
existingModelsAudited.reason: Wrong domain entirely - this is about legal correctness of a conclusion Headroom has already made, not about Headroom's own inability to make one.

existingModelsAudited.scope: The OLDER onboarding-extraction pipeline (Phase 1/2): DEFINED_TERM/PERMISSION/RELATIONSHIP/etc. candidates proposed by extraction, reviewed by a human, promoted into Permission/etc. rows. FK'd to ExtractionRun/ExtractionStage.
existingModelsAudited.reused: PATTERN reused, not the models themselves
existingModelsAudited.reason: This is the closest proven precedent for exactly the shape this phase needs (proposed value never overwritten, append-only decision log, reviewedBy never fabricated, REVIEW_REQUIRED baked into the status vocabulary) - but it is FK'd to the wrong pipeline (the older 6-stage onboarding extraction pipeline, not the live 2A-3E contract-model compiler pipeline) and its ExtractionCandidateKind enum (DEFINED_TERM/PERMISSION/RELATIONSHIP/...) describes onboarding candidate TYPES, not covenant-claim safe-failure reasons. Extending ExtractionCandidateKind or FK'ing into ExtractionRun/ExtractionStage would conflate two genuinely different systems. The NEW ClaimReviewItem/ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision models reuse the exact proven SHAPE (see prisma/schema.prisma's own extensive comment on this) with correct FKs (Company/Document directly) and a correct, compiler-pipeline-specific reason/stage vocabulary.

existingModelsAudited.scope: The LEGACY Phase C orchestrator's own run/stage state machine.
existingModelsAudited.reason: orchestrator.ts's own header comment: 'NOT repaired here - quarantine only. app/** must never import [it]' - this is explicitly quarantined, dead-end infrastructure per Phase 3F.1.4's own legacy-quarantine work (tests/foundation-audit/legacy-phase-c-quarantine.test.ts). FK'ing a new production-critical safety feature into quarantined infrastructure would be a serious architectural mistake. Confirmed via code inspection that the LIVE pipeline (discovery/context-retrieval/amendment/semantic/semantic-verification/semantic-coverage) has NO persisted run/stage tracking table at all today (docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md: 'every run recomputes from scratch') - this phase's new enum ClaimReviewPipelineStage is therefore a fresh, minimal, correctly-scoped stage vocabulary naming the actual live module boundaries, not a reuse of the dead one.

existingModelsAudited.scope: A structured, richly-provenanced finding produced by ONE stage (the verifier) about ONE candidate.
existingModelsAudited.reused: conceptually, via the emission-point design, not schema-duplicated
existingModelsAudited.reason: Already has nearly every field ClaimReviewItem needs (candidateRef, findingType, severity, sourceEvidence, sourceCitation, verifierReasoning, resolutionStatus) - but it is scoped to ONE stage's output only, in-memory/JSON (never persisted as first-class DB state today), and cannot by itself satisfy Section 11's cross-stage dedup requirement (a verifier finding and a compiler failure for the SAME claim are two separate SemanticVerificationFinding-shaped or SemanticCompilationResult-shaped objects with no shared persisted identity linking them). ClaimReviewItem's role is precisely to be the cross-stage aggregation point these per-stage models feed into, not a replacement for them.

existingModelsAudited.scope: The reconciliation engine's own per-unit safety verdict, already independently combining discovery+compiler+verifier evidence.
existingModelsAudited.reused: DIRECTLY - this is the actual source of truth ClaimReviewItem is derived from
existingModelsAudited.reason: This is the single biggest discovery of this phase's design work: Phase 3E ALREADY computes almost everything this phase's charter asks for (a coverage-state taxonomy nearly isomorphic to the required review-status model, a dangerous-unaccounted-reason taxonomy nearly isomorphic to the required reasonCode model, and a stable, sibling-safe, content-derived claim identity via MaterialSemanticUnit.semanticUnitId). What Phase 3E's own runSemanticCoverageAudit() never did is PERSIST this signal as durable, lifecycle-bearing, queryable production state - it is called only from offline scripts and tests (grep-verified: zero live app/ callers), producing an in-memory report object that is discarded after each run. This phase's entire contribution is exactly that: promoting an already-correct, already-real computation into first-class, durable, reviewable, resolvable production state - which is precisely what Section 3's 'do not duplicate existing review models if one can be safely generalized' instructs.

moduleLayout.prismaModels: prisma/schema.prisma - ClaimReviewItem, ClaimReviewObservation, ClaimReviewDecision + 4 supporting enums (ClaimReviewStatus, ClaimReviewReasonCode, ClaimReviewPipelineStage, ClaimReviewDecisionAction). Migration 20260829232147_phase_3f1_5_r_claim_review_safe_failure, additive only.
moduleLayout.domainLayer: lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/ - types.ts (domain types), identity.ts (claim-key derivation, reusing semantic-coverage's semanticUnitId or the compiler's own candidateRef), derive.ts (pure derivation from an already-computed SemanticUnitCoverageEntry - zero new semantic judgment), service.ts (persistence + dedup + resolution lifecycle + the Section 15 evaluator-compatibility function), integrate.ts (the one wired emission point, called explicitly after runSemanticCoverageAudit()).

productionInvariantEncoded: NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE: for every MaterialSemanticUnit at CRITICAL/MATERIAL tier whose SemanticUnitCoverageEntry is not FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED, deriveFromCoverageEntry() either returns a ClaimReviewItemInput (which service.ts persists) or explicitly documents why not (below-material-tier, missing anchor). No code path silently discards this signal.
